intro.heading: From marketecture to running system
paragraphs: OneTrust's AI Governance wedge, as Sriram has framed it, is Platform + Solutions: detect(), assess(), act(), attest() running on a Trust Graph. The functional architecture below is one engineer's answer to a specific question: what does that actually take to build, layer by layer, from the customer-facing surface down to the cloud foundation.

Seven layers. Two functions tagged explicitly: CPS (Core Platform & Solutions) for what exists in production today, AEP (AI Platform & Emerging Products) for what the new business builds, plus a stable facade contract where both sides meet and hand off work without either blocking the other or duplicating effort.

layers.title: CPS Enterprise Solutions
layers.description: The customer-facing solution suite in production today.

layers.title: CPS Experience & Developer Surface
layers.description: How customers and partners reach every solution.

layers.title: Dual Enterprise Capability Facade
layers.description: A stable contract implemented by both CPS and AEP. Business services consume capabilities through this contract, which is what lets the two organizations evolve independently without breaking each other.

layers.title: AEP Enterprise Context Layer
layers.description: The proposed area of direct ownership. Unifies identity, meaning, and policy across every silo the platform touches, and serves it as governed, queryable context.

components.name: Match Engine
components.detail: Deterministic + probabilistic matching across sources.
components.example: Matches "J. Smith" in the HR system to "Jane Smith" in the CRM as one data subject.

components.name: Golden Record Builder
components.detail: Merges matched records into one canonical entity.
components.example: Builds one Vendor record from 3 duplicate entries created by separate onboarding forms.

components.name: Survivorship Rules
components.detail: Resolves conflicting attribute values.
components.example: Keeps the legal entity name from the contract system over a stale value in the CRM.

components.name: Identity Registry
components.detail: Stores resolved entity IDs and cross-references.
components.example: Maps a customer's 4 regional account IDs to one global entity ID.

components.name: Lineage Capture
components.detail: Records source, transform, and load steps per fact.
components.example: Tags a risk score as derived from "Vendor Assessment v3, field Q12."

components.name: Provenance Store
components.detail: Immutable log of fact origin and change history.
components.example: Shows a consent flag was set by the CMP webhook on a specific date.

components.name: Impact Analysis
components.detail: Traces downstream effects of a source change.
components.example: Flags 40 assessments that reference a regulation clause just amended.

components.name: Domain Ontology
components.detail: Canonical business vocabulary and entity types.
components.example: Defines "Processing Activity" once, used consistently by Privacy and AI Governance.

components.name: Term Mapping
components.detail: Aligns solution-specific terms to shared vocabulary.
components.example: Maps "Data Subject" (Privacy) and "End User" (Consent) to the same entity type.

components.name: Schema Registry
components.detail: Versioned schemas for context objects.
components.example: Publishes v2 of the "AI System" context schema without breaking v1 consumers.

components.name: Graph Store
components.detail: Entities and relationships, queryable at scale.
components.example: Stores Vendor → Processes → Dataset → Subject-to → Regulation as linked nodes.

components.name: Relationship Extractor
components.detail: Derives relationships from source data and events.
components.example: Infers a new Vendor-to-Subprocessor link from an updated DPA document.

components.name: Graph Query API
components.detail: Traversal and pattern-match queries.
components.example: Answers "which AI systems touch EU customer data" in one query.

components.name: Graph Refresh Pipeline
components.detail: Incremental updates from source changes.
components.example: Re-links a dataset when its owning team changes in the source system.

components.name: Obligation Mapper
components.detail: Links regulatory/policy obligations to entities.
components.example: Attaches GDPR Art. 35 (DPIA required) to any AI system tagged high-risk.

components.name: Trust Scoring
components.detail: Computes trust/risk posture per entity.
components.example: Scores a vendor lower after two missed evidence submissions.

components.name: Policy Change Propagation
components.detail: Updates the graph when a policy source changes.
components.example: Re-flags 12 vendors when a new state privacy law adds a data category.

components.name: Query Planner
components.detail: Resolves a context request into graph + store lookups.
components.example: Plans the lookups needed to answer "assess this AI model's risk."

components.name: Composition Service
components.detail: Assembles multi-source context into one response.
components.example: Merges vendor risk + data inventory + policy graph into one context object.

components.name: Freshness & Versioning
components.detail: Point-in-time context snapshots.
components.example: Returns the context as it existed at the moment an assessment was submitted.

components.name: Access Control Layer
components.detail: Scopes context by caller, tenant, and purpose.
components.example: Hides another business unit's vendor data from a tenant-scoped caller.

layers.title: AEP Decision & Intelligence Layer
layers.description: Where governed context becomes an explainable decision. Every action traceable end to end: assess, act, attest.

components.name: Reasoning Engine
components.detail: Applies IDS-structured logic to assembled context.
components.example: Concludes a vendor needs re-assessment given a new subprocessor and an expired SOC 2.

components.name: Recommendation Generator
components.detail: Synthesizes next-best-action candidates.
components.example: Suggests "request updated DPA" and "flag for legal review" for a vendor.

components.name: Ranking & Prioritization
components.detail: Orders candidates by expected value/risk.
components.example: Surfaces the 5 highest-risk AI systems awaiting assessment first.

components.name: Task Planner
components.detail: Decomposes a goal into ordered agent steps.
components.example: Breaks "onboard this vendor" into inventory check, risk scan, then DPA request.

components.name: Agent Runtime
components.detail: Governed sandbox for agent execution.
components.example: Runs the onboarding agent with read-only access until a human approves writes.

components.name: Tool / Skill Registry
components.detail: Catalog of actions an agent may invoke.
components.example: Lists "send assessment," "update risk score," "create task" as callable tools.

components.name: Human-in-the-Loop Gate
components.detail: Routes high-risk actions for approval.
components.example: Holds an auto-generated policy exception for a compliance officer to sign off.

components.name: Assess Log
components.detail: What context and rules were evaluated.
components.example: Logs which policy clauses and risk factors were checked for a given decision.

components.name: Act Log
components.detail: What action was taken and by what trigger.
components.example: Records that a vendor was auto-suspended after a failed evidence deadline.

components.name: Attest Log
components.detail: Signed record of the full decision chain.
components.example: Produces an auditor-ready record of how a risk score was reached.

components.name: Context Trace Viewer
components.detail: Human-readable replay of a decision.
components.example: Lets a reviewer step through why an AI system was flagged high-risk.

components.name: Model Router
components.detail: Selects model/provider per request profile.
components.example: Routes a sensitive PII-review task to an approved, audited model only.

components.name: Prompt & Guardrail Enforcement
components.detail: Applies policy constraints pre/post-call.
components.example: Blocks a prompt that would leak another tenant's assessment data.

components.name: Response Validator
components.detail: Checks output against expected schema/policy.
components.example: Rejects a model response that omits a required risk-justification field.

components.name: Online Signal Processor
components.detail: Real-time event-driven scoring inputs.
components.example: Reacts within minutes to a breach-notification webhook from a vendor.

components.name: Offline Feature Fusion
components.detail: Governed batch features from the catalog.
components.example: Pulls last quarter's audit findings as a scoring feature.

components.name: Composite Score Calculator
components.detail: Combines online + offline into one score.
components.example: Blends a live incident signal with historical audit score into one risk rating.

components.name: Outcome Capture
components.detail: Records accepted / declined / expired outcomes.
components.example: Notes that a compliance officer declined the "auto-suspend vendor" suggestion.

components.name: Model Tuning Pipeline
components.detail: Feeds outcomes back into scoring/reasoning.
components.example: Down-weights a signal that reviewers consistently override.

components.name: Drift Monitor
components.detail: Flags degrading recommendation quality.
components.example: Alerts when acceptance rate for a recommendation type drops below threshold.

layers.title: CPS Existing Core Platform
layers.description: The multi-tenant substrate already in production.

layers.title: AEP Platform Extensions
layers.description: Extends the core platform with what AI-native solutions need: retrieval, memory, agents, and observability, all governed.

components.name: Insight Aggregator
components.detail: Rolls up cross-domain findings into summaries.
components.example: Produces a weekly "top 10 emerging vendor risks" digest for leadership.

components.name: Alerting Service
components.detail: Notifies on emerging risk or opportunity patterns.
components.example: Pages the compliance team when 3+ vendors miss the same control in a month.

components.name: Embedding Generator
components.detail: Produces vector representations of content.
components.example: Embeds every policy clause so it can be matched to relevant assessments.

components.name: Vector Index Manager
components.detail: Maintains searchable embedding indices.
components.example: Keeps the regulation-text index current as new clauses are published.

components.name: Retriever
components.detail: Fetches relevant context/documents for a query.
components.example: Pulls the 3 most relevant DPA clauses for a vendor risk question.

components.name: Augmentation Assembler
components.detail: Merges retrieved content into the model prompt.
components.example: Adds the retrieved clauses to the prompt before generating a risk summary.

components.name: Offline Eval Suite
components.detail: Benchmark tests run pre-deployment.
components.example: Checks a new reasoning model against 200 labeled risk-assessment cases.

components.name: Online Eval Monitor
components.detail: Live quality sampling in production.
components.example: Spot-checks 1 in 20 live recommendations against reviewer judgment.

components.name: Policy Rule Engine
components.detail: Encodes allowed/blocked behaviors.
components.example: Blocks any agent action that would auto-approve a vendor above risk threshold.

components.name: Content Safety Filter
components.detail: Screens inputs and outputs for violations.
components.example: Strips PII from a response before it's logged or displayed.

components.name: MCP Server Interface
components.detail: Exposes tools/context to agents via MCP.
components.example: Lets a third-party agent call "get vendor risk" through a governed MCP tool.

components.name: Agent SDK
components.detail: Common libraries for building governed agents.
components.example: Gives engineers a standard pattern for building a new assessment agent.

components.name: Short-Term Memory Store
components.detail: Session-scoped working context.
components.example: Remembers the vendor being discussed across a multi-turn conversation.

components.name: Long-Term Memory Store
components.detail: Persisted, retrievable interaction history.
components.example: Recalls that this vendor was flagged for the same issue 6 months ago.

components.name: Telemetry Collector
components.detail: Captures latency, cost, and usage metrics.
components.example: Tracks per-model token cost across all AI governance workflows.

components.name: Trace & Debug Console
components.detail: Inspects individual model/agent calls.
components.example: Lets an engineer replay the exact prompt that produced a bad recommendation.

layers.title: Dual Shared Data & Knowledge Platform
layers.description: The shared substrate both organizations read and write.

layers.description: The infrastructure layer everything else runs on.

workSample.heading: Asset Intelligence (Stealth Mode): the same architecture discipline, shipped
workSample.description: Asset Intelligence is a production system scoring media assets against brand, brief, and provenance requirements: five scorers, a compliance engine, chain-of-custody tracking. It shows the same architecture pattern proposed for OneTrust's Context Layer, already built and running: a foundation-model API called through typed, structured tool contracts rather than free text, an orchestrator that selects and sequences scorers, and a closed evaluation loop.
workSample.evolutionNote: The two diagrams below chart the same evolution the OneTrust proposal is built on: from siloed trained models, to a single general-purpose model called directly, to an orchestrator with retrieval and closed-loop evaluation around it. This is the architecture pattern behind Reasoning & Recommendations, Agent Orchestration, and the Feedback & Outcome Loop layers above.
